§6Short-Lived Nuclear Waste§f

§aSeven flavors of radioactive garbage, each with different recycling yields. Sort them carefully.§f

§bShort-Lived Nuclear Waste§f comes from fission products with relatively short half-lives. There are §e7 sub-classes§f based on source: U-233, U-235, Np-237, Pu-239, Pu-240, Pu-241, and Sa-326.

§6How You Get It§f: Extract from spent fuel using a §bSILEX§f. Each fuel type produces its corresponding waste class.

§6Decay Yields§f (put in §bNuclear Waste Disposal Drum§f):
§b•§f §bU-233§f → Zirconium, Dust, Lead, U-238, Bismuth
§b•§f §bU-235§f → Zirconium, Dust, Lead, U-238, Bismuth
§b•§f §bNp-237§f → Zirconium, Dust, U-238, Lead
§b•§f §bPu-239§f → Zirconium, Dust, Lead, U-238
§b•§f §bPu-240§f → Zirconium, Dust, Bismuth, Lead, U-238
§b•§f §bPu-241§f → Bismuth, Dust, Lead
§b•§f §bSa-326§f → Bismuth, Mercury, Cerium, Lanthanum, Dust

§6Fresh (Non-Decayed)§f: Yields different isotopes, including Pu-238, Sr-90, I-131, Cs-137, and more. Check the full table on the wiki.

§cWARNING:§f Pyrophoric when not decayed! Handle with care or automate the entire chain.

Americium-242m type is currently unobtainable.
